label: positive

blockers.detail: Commit dbd4c441 added ARES_EDESTRUCTION handling which calls end_hquery(hquery, status), but FORGOT to return. Code continues to execute and may call end_hquery() again in the 'if (!hquery->remaining)' block below, causing double-free of hquery. This is triggered when ares_destroy() is called while ares_getaddrinfo() is in progress.

evidence: Commit dbd4c441 adds 'else if (status == ARES_EDESTRUCTION) { end_hquery(hquery, status); }' without return
Fix commit 1cc7e83c (reported by Jann Horn @ Google Project Zero) adds 'return;' after end_hquery()
Fix commit message: 'would result in an invalid read and double-free due to calling end_hquery() twice'
OSS-Fuzz has ares_getaddrinfo_fuzzer which can trigger ares_destroy() during operation

rationale.zh: c-ares改进了ares_getaddrinfo的实现，添加了ARES_EDESTRUCTION状态的处理来支持在操作进行中调用ares_destroy()。代码调用end_hquery()释放资源，但忘记return，导致代码继续执行到下面的if块，可能再次调用end_hquery()，造成double-free。这个问题在fuzzing时如果调用ares_destroy()就会触发，导致crash。Google Project Zero的Jann Horn报告了这个安全问题。这是典型的生命周期管理错误：资源已释放但控制流继续执行导致再次释放。属于显式lifecycle类退化（ASan立即检测）。
rationale.en: c-ares improved ares_getaddrinfo implementation by adding ARES_EDESTRUCTION handling to support calling ares_destroy() during operation. The code calls end_hquery() to free resources but forgets to return, causing execution to continue to the if block below, potentially calling end_hquery() again and causing double-free. This is triggered during fuzzing if ares_destroy() is called, causing crashes. Reported by Jann Horn @ Google Project Zero as a security issue. This is a classic lifecycle management error: resource freed but control flow continues, causing re-free. Explicit lifecycle degradation (ASan detects immediately).
